definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sliding door made of a wooden lattice frame covered with translucent washi paper. Used as room dividers and exterior doors in traditional Japanese architecture.

examples.japanese: {障子戸|しょうじど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えた→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: When I opened the shoji door, I could see the garden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{障子戸|しょうじど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{穴|あな}→穴：01691_ana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けて→開ける：00563_akeru⟧しまった。

examples.english: Soft light was streaming in through the shoji doors of the old inn.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧ (shoji screen) and {戸|ど} (door). While ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧ alone often refers to the same thing, {障子戸|しょうじど} specifically emphasizes its function as a door (opening/closing to enter/exit). The translucent paper allows soft, diffused light to pass through while providing privacy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {障子戸|しょうじど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ — to open the shoji door
- {障子戸|しょうじど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧ — to close the shoji door
- {障子戸|しょうじど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{張|は}り{替|か}え — re-papering of shoji doors

CULTURAL NOTE:
Shoji doors are a defining feature of traditional Japanese houses (⟦{和室|わしつ}→和室：10437_washitsu⟧). The paper is typically replaced annually, often at year-end cleaning (⟦{大掃除|おおそうじ}→大掃除：08347_oosouji⟧). In modern homes, glass or acrylic panels sometimes replace the traditional ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧ — shoji (the screen/panel itself, often used interchangeably)
- ⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧ — fusuma (opaque sliding door, thicker and painted, used between rooms)
- ⟦{引|ひ}き{戸|ど}→引き戸：27509_hikido⟧ — sliding door (general term for any sliding door)
